questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes ethics from integrity?
options: They mean exactly the same thing.
Ethics gives principles for right and wrong; integrity is consistently acting on them.
Integrity is about laws and ethics is about feelings.
Ethics applies to employees and integrity applies to owners.
questions.explanation: The notes: ethics helps us understand what we should do; integrity is demonstrated when we consistently act according to those principles.

questions.question: An owner knows falsifying records is wrong but falsifies them under financial pressure. What does this show?
options: The owner understands the ethics but fails the test of integrity.
The owner has acted ethically because the business survived.
Falsifying records is only a legal problem.
questions.explanation: Knowing the principle (ethics) and acting on it consistently (integrity) are different. Integrity is tested when the right decision is costly.

questions.question: In the small factory dilemma, how many jobs are at risk if nothing changes, and how many would retrenching preserve?
questions.explanation: All 20 employees may lose their jobs; retrenching 5 would keep the business alive and preserve 15 jobs.

questions.question: Selling customer data would save jobs but the customers never gave permission. Which lens objects most directly?
options: Outcomes, because jobs would be lost
Principles and rights, because it violates consent, privacy and trust
Profit, because the data has no value
questions.explanation: The outcomes lens may support the sale (it saves jobs), but the principles and rights lens points to privacy, consent and customer trust.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the four factors that push people towards unethical behaviour in the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes give pressure, opportunity, justification and incentives.

questions.question: A business receives P10,000 cash and records only P6,000. Which is a likely consequence listed in the class?
options: Poor management decisions and loss of trust
questions.explanation: The consequences listed are inaccurate financial information, poor management decisions, weak internal controls, loss of trust and compliance problems.

questions.question: Which group does the chapter treat as primary stakeholders?
questions.explanation: Owners, customers and employees interact directly with the business, so they are the primary stakeholders.

questions.question: A business delays paying a small supplier for six months without telling it. What is the main ethical concern in the notes?
options: It may simply move financial pressure from one business to another.
Suppliers do not matter to a business.
questions.explanation: Suppliers may themselves be small businesses; delaying payment without communication can transfer the pressure and may harm them.

questions.question: Which pair correctly describes legal and ethical responsibility?
options: Legal is the minimum standard; ethical goes further than the law.
Ethical is the minimum standard; legal goes further.
Legal applies to big firms only.
questions.explanation: Legal responsibility sets a minimum standard of conduct. An action can be legal and still raise ethical concerns.

questions.question: What do the PRO factors stand for?
questions.explanation: Product, Representatives and Organisation are the legitimate ways to build confidence instead of using a legitimacy lie.

questions.question: Which is a benefit of integrity in the lecturer's list of eight?
questions.explanation: Reduced employee turnover is on the list. Trust is the mechanism in the integrity chain, not one of the eight benefits.

questions.question: Which sequence matches the Class 2 integrity chain?
options: Integrity, trust, stronger relationships, loyalty, reputation, long-term sustainability
questions.explanation: Integrity can strengthen trust, relationships, loyalty and reputation, which support long-term sustainability.

questions.question: The textbook and the notes list six steps in one cut, and Class 2 slide 28 in another. What is the difference at step 4 and step 5?
options: The notes separate "make the decision" and "implement it"; slide 28 has a separate principles, fairness and rights step and merges make and implement.
Slide 28 has more than six steps.
questions.explanation: Notes and textbook: define, alternatives, evaluate, make, implement, evaluate. Slide 28: define, alternatives, consequences and stakeholders, principles fairness and rights, make and implement, review.

questions.question: Which question belongs to the Class 2 quick ethical test?
options: Would I be comfortable explaining the decision publicly?
questions.explanation: The quick test asks: is it truthful, fair to those affected, would I be comfortable explaining it publicly, will it strengthen or damage relationships, and have I considered alternatives that reduce harm.

questions.question: What are the three parts of the triple bottom line?
questions.explanation: People, Profit and Planet. Purpose, Pride and Patience belong to the five principles of an ethical culture.
